newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan parliament committee passes 1997/98 budget.
newsitem.headline: Japan parliament committee passes 1997/98 budget.

text.p: The key budget committee of the Lower House of Japan's parliament on Wednesday approved a state budget totalling 77.39 trillion yen for the fiscal year starting on April 1, a parliamentary official said.
A full session of the Lower House is expected to approve the budget later on Wednesday, and it will then be sent to the Upper House for debate.
Since the Lower House has authority concerning the budget, its approval means that passage is virtually assured.

Despite calls by opposition parties for cuts in spending to reduce government debt, the budget was approved without revision on the strength of voting by the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) and two parties that have a loose alliance with it.
The budget for 1997/98, which Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto has said will be the first year of fiscal reforms, was 3.0 percent larger than last fiscal year's original budget.
The original l996/97 budget was bigger by 5.8 percent than the year before.

The budget has been the subject of criticism by financial markets and the general public because it features tax increases and the possibility of more spending to build new lines for Shinkansen bullet trains in the future.
